title: Inspection, Search, Seizure and Arrest
outcomes: Apply search and seizure powers and safeguards.

meta.exam_tip: Name the authorising officer, the threshold and the safeguard for each power.

concepts.title: Inspection
body: Section 67(1): an officer not below Joint Commissioner may authorise inspection of a business place, or a transporter's or warehouse premises, on reasons to believe that a taxpayer hid supplies or stock, claimed excess ITC, contravened the Act to evade tax, or a transporter or warehouse keeper is handling goods that escaped tax or keeps accounts so as to aid evasion.
Authorisation is given in writing (INS-01). Inspection is less intrusive than search and is directed at verifying records and goods.
Reasons to believe must be based on credible material, not mere suspicion.
concepts.analogy: Inspection is a look; search is a hunt.
concepts.work: Suspected stock suppression can lead to inspection of a godown.

concepts.title: Search and seizure
body: Section 67(2): where the Joint Commissioner has reasons to believe goods liable to confiscation or documents relevant to proceedings are hidden, he may authorise search and seizure. Goods may be seized; if seizure is not practicable, a prohibitory order (INS-04) may be issued.

Safeguards: seized documents are retained only as long as needed; the person may take copies; a notice regarding seized goods must be issued within six months (extendable by six months) or the goods returned; goods may be released provisionally on bond and security or on payment of tax, interest and penalty; searches follow the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita provisions, with witnesses and an inventory.
Perishable or hazardous goods may be disposed of; section 68 empowers inspection of goods in movement with prescribed documents.
concepts.analogy: Search requires strong reasons and comes with safeguards.
concepts.work: Goods seized on 1 May must get a notice by 1 November unless the period is extended.

concepts.title: Arrest and its safeguards
body: Section 69: the Commissioner may authorise arrest if he has reason to believe a person committed offences under section 132(1)(a) to (d) (fake invoices, supplies without invoice, wrongful ITC or refunds) involving tax above ₹2 crore, or a repeat offender regardless of amount.

Offences with tax above ₹5 crore are cognizable and non-bailable; others are non-cognizable and bailable. For cognizable offences, the person is informed of the grounds and produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours; for bailable offences, the Deputy or Assistant Commissioner can release on bail.
Procedural safeguards include recording reasons, informing a nominated person, and medical examination where needed.
concepts.analogy: Arrest is reserved for serious or repeat fraud.
concepts.work: An evasion of ₹1.2 crore by a first offender does not justify arrest.

concepts.title: Summons, access and production of records
body: Section 70: a proper officer may summon any person to give evidence or produce documents in an inquiry; the proceedings are judicial proceedings for IPC/BNS purposes, and persons summoned may appear through authorised representatives where permitted.

Section 71: an officer authorised by the Joint Commissioner may access any business place of a registered person to inspect books, documents, computers and records; the person must produce records such as audited accounts, cost audit reports, income-tax audit reports and other prescribed documents within 15 working days.
Section 72 requires government officers, police, railways and others to assist GST officers.
concepts.analogy: Summons and access support investigation without search.
concepts.work: An officer may visit a business and ask for audited accounts under section 71.

jobs.title: Search response protocol
jobs.situation: GST officers arrive with a search authorisation.
steps: Track six-month notice deadline and seek provisional release.
jobs.takeaway: Knowing the safeguards protects the business during searches.

viva.q: What is the difference between inspection and search?
viva.model: Inspection verifies records and goods; search looks for hidden goods or documents and allows seizure.

viva.q: How can seized goods be released provisionally?
viva.model: On executing a bond with security, or on payment of tax, interest and penalty.

viva.q: Who can grant bail for a bailable GST offence?

viva.model: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 provisions on searches.

viva.q: Name two records producible under section 71.
viva.model: Audited annual accounts and the income-tax audit report.
